steps.body: An area model stacks the groups as rows: four rows each showing 3/8 shades twelve eighth-pieces in all.
steps.narration: An area model stacks the groups as rows: four rows each showing 3/8 shades twelve eighth-pieces in all.

widget.successFeedback: 12/8 — twelve eighth-pieces, which is one and a half wholes.
widget.lowFeedback: Your shaded bar is shorter than the target half. Shade more — raise the numerator, or use fewer parts.
widget.highFeedback: Your shaded bar is longer than half. Shade less — lower the numerator, or split into more parts.

commonFractions.feedback: 12/12 read the answer as a single whole; twelve EIGHTHS is one and a half wholes.
3/8 is one row. Four rows were shaded.

predict.prompt: Four rows each shading 3/8 — do the pieces get smaller?
predict.reveal: Each row is a copy of the same whole cut into eighths; stacking copies never re-cuts the pieces.

cml.actionGoal: Collect equal groups of a fraction and watch only the COUNT of pieces change for g4x area model.
invariants: Multiplying a fraction by a whole number collects groups of identical pieces: the denominator names the piece size and holds still, while the numerator counts every piece gathered, which is what keeps g4x area model a counting problem.
misconceptions: Scaling the denominator along with the numerator, adding the whole number to the numerator, or assuming a product cannot pass one whole.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the denominator DID change when you collected groups, what would happen to the size of each piece?

widget.prompt: An area model for 4 × 3/8 shows four rows, each with 3 of 8 parts shaded. What does the shading total?

options.label: 12/8, because 12 eighth-pieces are shaded
options.feedback: Correct — four rows of three eighths shade twelve eighths in all, which is one and a half wholes.

options.label: 12/32, because there are 32 parts in all
options.feedback: The pieces are still eighths of ONE whole; stacking rows does not shrink the piece size.

options.label: 7/8, because 4 + 3 = 7
options.feedback: Adding the group count to the numerator mixes two different quantities.

options.label: 3/8, because each row shows 3/8
options.feedback: That is one row. The model has four of them, and the question asks for the total shaded.
